Item: Sperm take about 2 and a half months to develop.
What the patient sees or answers: A sperm cell takes over 70 days to grow and mature. So anything that harms sperm, or stops harming them, takes about 3 months to show up in a sample.
Source(s): ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Optimizing Male Fertility (2023)

What the patient sees or answers: The testicles hang outside the body to stay a few degrees cooler than the rest of you, because sperm develop best at 97 to 99 degrees. Hot tubs, saunas, and a laptop resting on the lap all add heat.
Source(s): Cleveland Clinic: Male Reproductive System (2023-05-08) | ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Optimizing Male Fertility (2023)

Item: Taking testosterone or anabolic steroids shuts down sperm production.
What the patient sees or answers: Outside testosterone switches off the brain signals that tell the testicles to make sperm, often driving counts very low or to zero. Production usually returns over about 3 to 12 months after stopping.
Source(s): ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Testosterone Use and Male Infertility (2021) | Cleveland Clinic: Can Drugs Lower Your Sperm Count? (2022-11-10)

What the patient sees or answers: THC can interfere with testosterone production, which sperm making depends on.
Source(s): Cleveland Clinic: Can Drugs Lower Your Sperm Count? (2022-11-10) | ASRM Practice Committee: Tobacco or Marijuana Use and Infertility (2024)

Item: Smoking speeds up the loss of eggs, and lost eggs do not come back.
What the patient sees or answers: Chemicals in cigarette smoke, including nicotine, cyanide, and carbon monoxide, speed up the rate eggs are lost. Menopause comes 1 to 4 years earlier in people who smoke.
Source(s): ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Smoking and Infertility (2023)

Item: Smoking lowers sperm count and movement.
What the patient sees or answers: Smoke chemicals can damage sperm DNA and increase the share of abnormally shaped sperm.
Source(s): ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Smoking and Infertility (2023) | ASRM Practice Committee: Tobacco or Marijuana Use and Infertility (2024)

Item: Egg supply is set at birth; age and egg count are not things anyone can change.
What the patient sees or answers: A person is born with all the eggs they will ever have. No treatment grows new ones. Of the everyday factors, smoking is the clearly proven harm to avoid.
Source(s): ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Does My Age Affect My Fertility? (2023) | ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Smoking and Infertility (2023)

Item: Long-term opioid use can lower sperm quantity and quality.
What the patient sees or answers: Opioids disrupt the brain signals that control testosterone.
Source(s): Cleveland Clinic: Can Drugs Lower Your Sperm Count? (2022-11-10)

Item: Heavy drinking is linked to reduced fertility.
What the patient sees or answers: ASRM defines heavy as more than 2 drinks a day. In men, heavy alcohol use can lower testosterone, which sperm production depends on.
Source(s): ASRM ReproductiveFacts.org: Optimizing Natural Fertility (2023) | Cleveland Clinic: Can Drugs Lower Your Sperm Count? (2022-11-10)

Item: Some popular advice has no evidence behind it.
What the patient sees or answers: There is no proof that fertility supplements work, and position or lying down after sex does not change the odds of conception. Skipping those saves money and worry.
